findings.title: Dynamic imports in `appStore` are evaluated eagerly at module load time
findings.body: In `packages/app-store/index.ts`, each property value is written as `import("./...")` directly inside the `appStore` object literal. In JavaScript, object property values are evaluated immediately when the object is constructed, so importing `@calcom/app-store` still triggers all 28 dynamic `import()` calls eagerly at module initialization time rather than loading only the requested app on demand. To defer loading until a specific app is accessed, wrap each import in a getter (`get applecalendar() { return import("./applecalendar"); }`) or a thunk (`applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`).

findings.title: Unawaited `forEach(async ...)` causes recurring event deletions to miss `apiDeletes`
findings.body: When cancelling all remaining bookings of a recurring event (lines 458-470), `.forEach(async (credential) => { ... })` is used. Because `forEach` does not await its `async` callback, execution suspends at `await getCalendar(credential)` and `await calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` before anything is pushed to `apiDeletes`. As a result, `apiDeletes` does not contain these deletion operations when `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (or `await apiDeletes`) runs, so the handler returns before recurring calendar events are deleted. This should iterate with `for (const credential of ...)` (as was done in the `else` branch on lines 480-483) or `Promise.all` with `.map`.

findings.title: `forEach(async ...)` inside `try/catch` does not await deletions or catch rejections
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` ignores the promises returned by the `async` callback. Because `getCalendar` is now awaited inside the callback, `calendar?.deleteEvent` is invoked asynchronously after the `try` block has already exited: any error thrown by `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting` will bypass the surrounding `try / catch` block as an unhandled promise rejection, and `Reschedule` will send emails and return without waiting for the calendar/video deletions. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))` instead.

findings.title: `forEach(async ...)` in `requestReschedule` does not await calendar and video deletions
findings.body: In `requestReschedule`, `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` does not await the `async` callback or the promises returned by `calendar?.deleteEvent` and `deleteMeeting`. With `await getCalendar(...)` added before `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`, the deletion call itself is now deferred until after `forEach` finishes, so the mutation sends reschedule emails, fires webhooks, and returns before calendar and video deletions have completed, and any rejection in the callback goes unhandled. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))`.
